title: Global univalence of the ergodic cylinder transformation on a periodic time scale (Theorem 3.5)
author: John M. Davis; Billy J. Jackson; Dylan Poulsen
work: Ergodic complex plane and cylinder transformation on a periodic time scale
source_version: Electronic Journal of Differential Equations 2026 (2026), No. 04, pp. 1--20; DOI 10.58997/ejde.2026.04; publisher version
difficulty_reason: The counted theorem is the article's central structural result: the averaged map xi-bar_{B^c}, already shown analytic and univalent off the branch cut in the retained Theorem 3.3, is extended across the branch cut B to a globally univalent xi-bar on the whole regressive complex plane. The extension is not a routine continuation, because B is the union of the intervals I_n between consecutive nonregressive points -1/mu_n determined by the graininess spectrum of the time scale. The proof must analyse the monotonicity of gamma_B on each I_n and locate the unique critical point alpha_n where gamma_B' vanishes, then choose interval by interval between xi-bar_{B^c}^+ and its negative so that the resulting piecewise xi-bar_B is injective, and finally verify injectivity across five distinct configurations of points, carrying the argument separately through the case of finitely many graininesses and the case of countably infinitely many. The analytic inputs - Karpuz's analyticity of the complex time-scale exponential and the Noshiro-Warschawski criterion - are named prerequisites supplied by the retained context, so the unit is H2 rather than H3; but the construction of the extension and its case analysis are source-local and are far outside an ordinary qualifying examination in complex analysis or in difference and dynamic equations.
